2610.08647.title: SquidAgent: Parallelize Wisely, Coordinate Efficiently
2610.08647.paper_summary: LLM-based agents solve complex multi-step tasks, but sequential execution incurs substantial latency. In principle, parallelizing work across multiple agents should yield near-linear speedups. Yet existing parallel multi-agent systems often run slower than a single-agent baseline. We attribute this gap to two hidden costs that parallel execution incurs but a serial agent avoids. First, there is a re-exploration cost: redundant effort spent by parallel workers reconstructing context that the orchestrator already possesses, such as prior decisions, that would otherwise be inherited implicitly in a serial execution. Second, there is an alignment cost: the overhead required to reconcile inconsistencies across independently generated outputs. We thus derive a principled decision criterion: a layer should be parallelized only when its critical-path cost, plus re-exploration and alignment overheads, is lower than the corresponding serial cost. While this criterion is naturally expressed in wall-clock time, we observe that LLMs are poorly calibrated when asked to estimate task duration. To address this, we instead measure cost in predicted output tokens, which we empirically find LLMs can estimate substantially more reliably than wall-clock time. Building on this token-based criterion, we propose SquidAgent. It estimates all token budgets in a single planning step, forks each worker directly from the orchestrator's session to eliminate re-exploration cost, and replaces post-hoc reconciliation with a pre-generated shared convention block that converts alignment into a bounded upfront cost. A deterministic scheduler then applies the criterion layer by layer. Empirically, SquidAgent achieves a 2.2$\times$ mean throughput improvement and a 2.6$\times$ mean wall-time speedup over Claude Code, and a 2.0$\times$ throughput improvement over the strongest multi-agent baseline.
2610.08647.paper_summary_zh: LLM 基礎的代理解決複雜的多步驟任務，但順序執行會產生相當大的延遲。原則上，將工作平行化到多個代理應該能實現接近線性的加速。然而，現有的平行多代理系統往往運行速度比單一代理基準還慢。我們將這一差距歸因於平行執行所產生的兩個隱藏成本，而串行代理則可以避免。首先，存在重新探索成本：平行工作者花費冗餘的努力重建指揮者已經擁有的上下文，例如先前的決策，這在串行執行中本來會隱式繼承。其次，還有對齊成本：調和獨立生成的輸出之間不一致所需的開銷。因此，我們推導出一個原則性的決策標準：只有當其關鍵路徑成本加上重新探索和對齊的開銷低於相應的串行成本時，層才應該被平行化。雖然這一標準自然以實時計算時間表達，但我們觀察到，當要求 LLM 預估任務持續時間時，其校準效果不佳。為了解決這個問題，我們改為以預測的輸出標記來衡量成本，我們實證發現 LLM 在這方面的預估可靠性遠高於實時計算時間。在這一基於標記的標準基礎上，我們提出了 SquidAgent。它在單一規劃步驟中估算所有標記預算，直接從指揮者的會話中分叉每個工作者，以消除重新探索成本，並用預生成的共享約定塊替換事後的調和，將對齊轉換為有界的前置成本。然後，確定性調度器逐層應用該標準。實證結果顯示，SquidAgent 在 Claude Code 上實現了 2.2$\times$ 的平均吞吐量提升和 2.6$\times$ 的平均實時計算時間加速，並在最強的多代理基準上實現了 2.0$\times$ 的吞吐量提升。
